assumptions: The CDS is in frame and a whole number of codons.
Tm is Biopython's `Tm_NN(strict=false)` under the named model, which is what upstream tiles against.
limits: Decides WHERE the primers sit, not which degenerate codon to use: one ambiguous codon is installed at every position.
A primer whose flanks cannot reach the Tm window inside the length limits is returned at the closest length upstream accepts, not dropped.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which primers tile this CDS, one degenerate codon per position, inside a Tm window?

description: Codon-tiling mutagenesis primers for a whole CDS: one primer per codon, each carrying a degenerate codon (NNN/NNK/NNS/NNC/NNG) at its centre, with the flanks grown or shrunk so every primer lands inside a Tm window (jbloomlab CodonTilingPrimers).

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

ambiguous_codon.description: the degenerate codon installed at every position. NNK and NNS halve the stop codons NNN introduces; NNC and NNG are narrower still.

cds.description: the CDS to tile, in frame. Left empty the record's `cds_feature`, or the selection, is tiled and the flanking bases come from the record around it.

cds_feature.description: tile this annotated CDS of the open record by NAME, on its own strand, exactly as `codon_usage_analysis` takes one. The flanks come from the record either side of it.

first_codon.description: the number given to the first codon in primer NAMES. Set it when the CDS you are tiling starts part-way through a protein. Advanced.

flanks.description: with a literal `cds`: the bases either side of it, as `5'flank,3'flank`. Upstream anneals every primer in these, so without them a tiled primer has nothing to grow into — give at least `(primer_length - 3) / 2` bases per side. Advanced.

max_length.description: longest primer it may grow to. In nt. Advanced.

max_primer_tm.description: highest acceptable primer Tm; must be above `min_primer_tm`. In °C.

min_length.description: shortest primer the flank search may shrink to. In nt. Advanced.

prefix.description: prefix for the generated primer names. Advanced.

primer_length.description: starting primer length, in bases. Must be ODD: the flanks are (n-3)/2 per side. Upstream's own default. In nt.

tm_model.description: Tm scale the window is judged on. Upstream tiles against Biopython's nearest-neighbour Tm, which is `santalucia` here. Values: santalucia (SantaLucia nearest-neighbor (Biopython Tm_NN defaults)), wallace (Wallace rule (4 °C per G·C, 2 °C per A·T)), gc:Chester_1993 (GC formula: Marmur-Doty (Chester & Marshak 1993)), gc:QuickChange (GC formula: QuikChange (the kit manufacturer’s own formula)), gc:Schildkraut_1965 (GC formula: Schildkraut & Lifson 1965 (Marmur-Doty + log[Na⁺])), gc:Wetmur_Melting_1991 (GC formula: Wetmur 1991, DNA (MELTING 4.3 approximate mode)), gc:Wetmur_RNA_1991 (GC formula: Wetmur 1991, RNA), gc:Wetmur_DNA_RNA_1991 (GC formula: Wetmur 1991, RNA/DNA hybrid), gc:Primer3 (GC formula: Primer3Plus product Tm (Biopython’s default set)), gc:Ahsen_2001 (GC formula: von Ahsen 2001 (accuracy against ease of use)).

name: design_codon_tiling_primers

count.description: primers designed, which is the number of codons tiled

outsideWindow.description: primers whose Tm the flank search could not bring inside the window within the length limits. Reported rather than dropped

primers.description: one row per codon: name, seq (with the degenerate codon at its centre), length, tm, codonIndex, and `start`, the 0-based offset in the tiled string

tmRange.description: the lowest and highest Tm actually achieved, against the window asked for: `{ min, max, wanted: { min, max } }`
